issue.title: Update: Node.js brute-force protection guidance
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The Node.js Security Cheat Sheet's brute-force section currently recommends Express-bouncer, express-brute, and rate-limiter. These examples are outdated and do not provide a good current reference for developers implementing rate limiting in Express applications.

The section also needs clearer guidance that rate limits should be applied to sensitive authentication endpoints and that distributed deployments may require shared rate-limit state.

## How should this be resolved?

- Replace the outdated package examples with a maintained, widely used open-source Express rate-limiting middleware.
- Add a short illustrative example for protecting a login endpoint.
- Explain that limits should be selected according to the protected endpoint and authentication flow.
- Mention the need for coordinated/shared state when rate limiting across multiple application instances.
- Keep the change focused to the existing brute-force guidance in `Nodejs_Security_Cheat_Sheet.md`.

This is intended as a focused update to existing guidance rather than a new cheat sheet.

Agreed. We want to keep away from detailed code samples that we cannot maintain well, and focus on architectural guidance. I think a new cheatsheet is prudent!

I went through the discussion and noticed that the current Node.js guidance mentions packages like `express-bouncer`, `express-brute`, and `rate-limiter`, while the proposal also raises the issue of shared rate-limit state in distributed deployments.

I saw the suggestion to move this into a separate Brute Force Cheat Sheet, and I think that makes sense if the goal is to keep the guidance useful across different stacks rather than tied to Node.js or specific middleware.

I'd be happy to help with this. Would you be open to assigning me the work once the scope is agreed, or would you prefer that I first open a separate issue for the new cheat sheet?

By doing that we will also not duplicate official documentations (which does nit make sense)

2890.title: docs: update Node.js CSRF protection guidance (#2797)
2890.body:
### Description

Updates the `Use Anti-CSRF tokens` subsection in the Node.js Security Cheat Sheet with focused, Node.js-specific CSRF protection guidance.

The change recommends using framework-provided CSRF protection where available, clarifies token validation for state-changing requests, and explains that `SameSite` cookies provide defense-in-depth rather than standalone protection. It also removes outdated guidance around the deprecated `csurf` package and links to the dedicated OWASP CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet.

The change is limited to this subsection. All surrounding guidance remains unchanged, including the brute-force section being handled separately under issue [[#2775](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2775)](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2775).
